assessment: This paper will be of interest to those interested in plant-microbe interactions under drought. Trees can exchange root exudates for minerals with soil bacteria. In a pot experiment under realistic conditions, the authors indicate that this exchange persists, and may be protective, when plants experience drought stress. The combination of methods used is an important strength: visualizing bacterial colonization of roots, measuring root exudation and mineral uptake, in conjunction with separate assays of bacterial growth responses to chemicals released by trees.
